annotation.title_clean: Chapter 634 (Senate Bill 720) – Education – Artificial Intelligence – Guidelines, Professional Development, and Collaborative (Artificial Intelligence Ready Schools Act)
annotation.title_en: Chapter 634 (Senate Bill 720) – Education – Artificial Intelligence – Guidelines, Professional Development, and Collaborative (Artificial Intelligence Ready Schools Act)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Maryland General Assembly (approved by Governor Wes Moore)
annotation.summary_en: Maryland's 2026 Artificial Intelligence Ready Schools Act requires the State Department of Education to issue AI guidance, a tool-evaluation rubric and teacher professional development. It requires local school systems to adopt AI policies and designate coordinators, and it creates a Maryland AI Education Collaborative. It covers software AI in K-12 only, not embodied AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Department of Education must publish AI guidance for students, educators, administrators and parents, and review it annually
Each local school system must adopt an AI policy within 120 days of the guidance and designate an AI coordinator
Department must publish a rubric for evaluating AI tools, and local systems must use it and procure under State procurement law
AI literacy must be added to workforce preparation and computer science standards by June 1, 2027, with teacher training
Creates the Maryland AI Education Collaborative, which reports annually from December 1, 2027; Section 2 expires May 31, 2028
